title: On that view man would never have lived forever without supernatural help
source_text: XXXIV. Si hanc, quae communior & probabilior est, sententiam sequamur, certum est hominem nunquam perpetuo victurum fuisse absque auxilio supernaturali. Nam immutatio illa per quam homo fuisset in vitam caelestem assumptus, non fuisset naturalis, sed supernaturalis.
pass_a_gloss: If we follow this opinion, which is more common and more probable, it is certain that man would never have lived perpetually without supernatural aid. For that change through which man would have been taken up into heavenly life would not have been natural, but supernatural.
pass_b_english: This opinion is both the more common and the more probable. On it, plainly, man could never have gone on living forever unless God helped him beyond nature, since the change that was to carry him up into heavenly life would itself have been a supernatural change, not a natural one.

choices.english: would have been not natural but supernatural
choices.why: Keeps the closing antithesis on which Le Blanc's view turns.
